items.evidence: Item.fuel comes only from the minecraft:cooking_fuel component (horizon-items/src/items.rs:1009-1011); 0/1416 items in 1.21.7 items.json carry it and no JSON in the tree defines it. Vanilla 1.21.7 has NO fuel component (DataComponents javap: 0 fuel refs); burn times are the hardcoded FuelValues.vanillaBurnTimes table (lava bucket 20000, coal block 16000, coal/charcoal 1600, #logs 300). Providers::burn_time is 0 for every item, so Furnace::tick never lights, menu.rs is_fuel is false (fuel slot refuses all fuel except buckets via is_bucket), and furnace quick-move fuel routing never fires. Furnace tick logic itself otherwise matches AbstractFurnaceBlockEntity.serverTick exactly.
items.title: Furnaces (furnace/blast furnace/smoker) can NEVER light: no fuel data in 1.21.7

items.evidence: brewing_fuel() (horizon-client-render/src/brewing.rs:423) reads only the minecraft:brewing_fuel component, absent in 1.21.7. Vanilla uses the #brewing_fuel item tag (blaze powder; tag EXISTS in the 1.21.7 jar data) + FUEL_USES=20 (BrewingStandBlockEntity.serverTick bytecode). Brew logic itself matches vanilla exactly (400 ticks, fuel-- on start, ingredient-identity reset, doBrew gating, bottle bits). Also breaks brewing quick-move fuel routing (blaze powder cannot be shift-clicked into the fuel slot).
items.title: Brewing stands can NEVER brew: fuel check reads an absent component

items.evidence: Rust burn() grows the output slot by recipe.result.count; vanilla AbstractFurnaceBlockEntity.burn() grows by exactly 1 when the slot is non-empty (javap ItemStack.grow(1)), full result copy only when empty. canBurn likewise: vanilla allows out.count < item max regardless of result count; Rust requires out.count + result.count <= max. Unreachable in vanilla data (all cooking recipes yield 1).
items.title: Furnace burn() grows output by the full result count; vanilla grows by 1 (datapack-only)

items.evidence: furnace.rs completes when cooking_timer >= cooking_total; vanilla serverTick completes only on == (bytecode 284-292, if_icmpne skip). With cookingTotalTime=0 (loaded save) vanilla never completes; Rust completes in 1 tick. A Rust test (loaded_totals_survive_until_actual_completion) pins the >= behaviour, contradicting vanilla bytecode. In test_furnace_loaded_total's scope ('zero' totals).
items.title: Furnace completion uses >= where vanilla uses == (loaded cookingTotalTime=0 completes in 1 tick)

items.evidence: furnace.rs pushes the fuel remainder to drops whenever one exists; vanilla only places the remainder when the fuel stack empties (serverTick bytecode 225-246), otherwise it is lost. Unreachable in vanilla data (only lava bucket has a remainder, max stack 1).
items.title: Furnace fuel remainder DROPPED when the fuel stack remains (datapack-only)

items.evidence: Vanilla serverTick resets cookingTimer to 0 when the lit furnace's input has no recipe (bytecode 341); Rust leaves it unchanged (no else on recipe lookup). Reachable only via datapack reload mid-cook / NBT edit (setItem resets on change).
items.title: Lit furnace + input with NO recipe keeps its cooking timer; vanilla resets it to 0

items.evidence: Vanilla SpawnEggItem.getType falls back to defaultType when ENTITY_DATA is empty (bytecode: getOrDefault(ENTITY_DATA, EMPTY) -> empty -> defaultType); the port's dispense_default_method drops the egg as an item (dispenser.rs). Reachable only via /data removing the component from a spawn egg.
items.title: Dispensed spawn egg with removed minecraft:entity_data drops as an item; vanilla spawns the default mob (commands-only corner)

items.evidence: hoppers_catch_items (entityInside path) uses the narrow INSIDE bowl (0.125..0.875, 11/16..1) while vanilla HopperBlockEntity.entityInside uses the full SUCK_AABB (0..1, 11/16..2). The tick path covers the full AABB, so pickup can only be 1-2 ticks late for fast items at the edges, never missed.
items.title: Hopper entity-catch uses the narrow bowl, not the full SUCK_AABB (pickup up to 1-2 ticks late at the edges)

items.evidence: crafter_eject only consults the block-only Containers::view (machines.rs:213), while vanilla CrafterBlockEntity.dispenseItem uses HopperBlockEntity.getContainerAt (block + entity). Dropper/hopper have the entity fallback; crafter lacks it. The result drops as an item instead.
items.title: Crafter never ejects into container ENTITIES (chest/hopper minecart, chest boat)

items.title: Crafter recipe_crafted trigger fires only for the host player (LAN-only)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 GameRules has NO spawner_blocks_work rule (javap: no RULE_SPAWNER_*); BaseSpawner.serverTick checks NO gamerule at all, and TrialSpawner.canSpawnInLevel checks only overridePeacefulAndMobSpawnRule || (difficulty != PEACEFUL && doMobSpawning) (javap). The port's gamerule table includes spawner_blocks_work defaulting true (gamerules.rs:114) and both Spawner::server_tick and TrialSpawner::can_spawn_in_level gate on it. Default play unaffected (defaults true), but the gate and the rule itself are 26.x carry-over; setting it false stops spawners in a way vanilla 1.21.7 cannot express.
items.title: Spawner + trial spawner ticking gated on non-vanilla 'spawner_blocks_work' gamerule

items.evidence: Vanilla EnchantmentMenu.clickMenuButton returns false when the lapis slot is EMPTY even in creative (itemstack.isEmpty() is outside the !hasInfiniteMaterials guard); the port's click_enchant skips the lapis-presence check entirely in creative. Survival behaviour matches (lapis count >= slot+1, level >= slot+1 and >= cost, deducts slot+1 levels).
items.title: Creative enchanting without lapis allowed; vanilla requires a lapis stack present

items.evidence: BlockEntity::for_block returns None for beds (not in container_size). Vanilla beds have BedBlockEntity (colour + custom name). Consequences: renamed beds lose their custom name on placement; /data get block on a bed returns nothing; chunk saves carry no bed BEs — explains the world-compare gap (bed blocks 50=50, bed BEs 0 vs 50). Colour itself is safe (per-block in 1.21.7).
items.title: No Bed block entity: renamed beds lose their name, chunk saves carry no bed BEs

items.evidence: open_ender_chest swaps the HOST's ender_items into the shared block BE; close copies back and leaves an empty Chest(27). A guest opening the same chest sees the host's items (while the host has it open) or an empty chest — never their own EnderItems. Host single-player behaviour is correct (player-specific inventory, block holds none).
items.title: Ender chest shows the wrong inventory to LAN guests (LAN-only)

items.evidence: Containers::view requires a BlockEntity in world.block_entities; pots have no variant (their item + sherds live in a spill saved tag), so view returns None. items.evidence: menu.rs carto_changed gates paper zoom on the minecraft:extendable_maps item tag, which does NOT exist in the 1.21.7 jar data (no data/minecraft/tags/item/extendable_maps.json). method: Static analysis only (execution-risk notice blocked all repo execution, git commands, cargo builds/tests and driver runs — Batch 2 precedent). Every behaviour check is javap -c on the named 1.21.7 server jar (~/workspace/mcir-work/leakage-audit/jars/1.21.7-server-named.jar) plus the Rust source and prepared data (~/workspace/mcir-work/mob-spawn/resources/). 57 driver checks triaged by reading each driver's assertions + the code it exercises; 34 method-2 checks (javap-vs-code, no driver). No driver was run; 'pass' means the static comparison found no divergence. 28 of the 43 gaps are 'driver cannot run (oracle broken)', not behaviour defects — see the oracle-defect items. No oracle repairs were attempted (repair requires editing repo Java + compiling to verify, both prohibited by the notice).
name: Block entities + containers
out_of_scope_failures: Excluded from the tally (other batches' scope): test_bonus_chest + test_decorated_region (worldgen), test_storage_alias (commands/Batch 10), test_food_storage (items/Batch 7), test_server_player_sculk (player/Batch 3), test_shulker_bullet (entity/Batch 3), test_held_item_stack (items/Batch 7). Unmeasured, excluded from the tally (no oracle exists and a live run is needed): test_disconnect_crafting (guest disconnect drop path not located statically), test_hive_default_patch (beehive save prototype elision not read). Not verified: sculk tick mechanics beyond save fields (oracle-blocked), command-block execution semantics (commands scope), full jukebox song lifecycle (driver disclaims it), recipe-book server packet construction (client side verified), trial spawner TIME_BETWEEN_EACH_EJECTION constant value (30, from vanilla source; javap shows it non-constant-folded). The save_roundtrip harness failure (launch + save-format divergence) is owned by the save harness, not this batch; only its BE touchpoint (bed BEs, B4-G13) is recorded here.
source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 4 + §3 methodology. Checks + triage only, no fixes. Scope: BE ticking/storage/render, menus, crafting/furnace/brewing logic; 47 BE types, 25 menus. Boundary note (Batch 10): test_sign_literal, test_storage_menu_parity and the recipe-book logic drivers count as Batch 4.
systemic_note: Three of the sixteen behaviour defects (B4-G01, B4-G02, B4-G16) share the pilot's systemic cause: the 1.21.7 port carries 26.x component/tag logic for lookups that do not exist in vanilla 1.21.7, and every such lookup silently degrades (fuel component absent from all 1416 items; brewing_fuel component absent where vanilla uses the #brewing_fuel tag; #extendable_maps tag absent where vanilla checks no tag at all). B4-G11 is the same pattern in the gamerule table (a 26.x-only rule gating spawner ticking). The prepared data is faithful to the jar — the port code, not the data, is the 26.x carry-over. The other thirteen defects are one-off logic divergences (ordering, rounding, missing fallbacks, LAN-only scoping). Oracle breakage is also systemic: 26 of the batch's oracles fail, mostly on 26.x-only packages (gamerules, gizmos, client/renderpearl/blaze3d) or 26.x API shapes — the oracle suite was written against 26.3 and needs a 1.21.7 retarget, not per-oracle fixes alone.
